surfaces.part: screen and button panel on front face

answer.evidence: Rows 1-4 are a light band across the full 28px width. Row 5 is a gray line darker than its neighbours and works as a front-edge line. Rows 6-7 are a short white lip with blue notches. Row 8 is a lighter blue line and row 9 is a dark shadow line, so the white band reads as a top surface over the front face. Below it the blue front face (screen, slot, buttons, base) runs from about row 8 to row 29, well over 3 rows. No receding side face is drawn. The call is borderline: the white band could instead be a face-on header sign, which would make this front_elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is two small ticket machines with a blue-grey body, a white panel and a screen. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, which matches the sticker look of a uniform near-black outline. The references that have tinted outlines (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%, well 33%) are the Beodeul standard, and the lamp's 100% is a thin pole. Body ramps show about 3 distinct steps (dark outline, mid blue, light panel) against 5-6 in the references. Visible tones per tile are 11, which is comparable to the hedge (9) but well below the stall (17) and well (20). There is no flat fill (0%), and small details such as the screen and buttons give some texture, but the large body surfaces are mostly smooth. Overall it is cleanly drawn but shallower than the references because of the neutral outline and the thin shading ramps.

surfaces.part: coin slot and ticket slot panel

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a 28px-wide rectangle spanning rows 0-29, with no widening or narrowing that would indicate an ellipse. The white band at rows 1-7 has a gray stripe at row 5. It is the same white above and below that stripe, and it ends in blue notches at rows 7-8. I read it as a front-facing sign header, not a horizontal top, because the white below the stripe does not look like a shaded face and no eave shadow follows an edge line. Everything below it is vertical: the screen at rows 9-15, the coin and ticket panel at rows 16-21, and the slot at rows 22-27. There is no side face. The machine reads as a flat front elevation with no readable top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is two small blue ticket machines with a dark grey outline all the way round. The measured facts back this up: 100% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline has no tint and reads as the uniform 'sticker' line. Only the lamp reference, a thin iron object, shares that neutral edge value; the hedge (0%), stall (1%) and well (33%) use tinted, material-toned darks. The body has about 4 lightness steps (shell, panel, screen, dark base), and the screen and keypad details are simple blocks. It has 11 visible tones per tile, which is close to the hedge (9) but below the stall (17) and well (20), the closest comparisons for a structured prop. There is no flat fill (0% near-flat), so the surface is not blank, but there is little grain, no per-material ramp and no material-coloured edge shading. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter, and the neutral outline is the main flaw.
